# SimpleINSURE Brokerage LLC

> Independent property and casualty insurance broker licensed in New York, Pennsylvania, and Florida (NY DFS BR-1984615). Principal also licensed in California. Office: 900 Stewart Ave Ste 210, Garden City, NY 11530; (516) 226-7969; info@simpleinsure.co. Serves Queens and the other New York City boroughs, Nassau County, and Suffolk County. We place insurance where we are licensed to do so. Those other license numbers are not listed here. If an account needs a license we do not hold, we say so before we proceed.

We place personal and commercial insurance for many industries. The specialty is the Real Estate Program: habitational property and general liability for landlords, mixed-use buildings, apartments, co-ops, and condos in New York, including Queens, and on Long Island. We also place coverage for contractors, restaurants, cafes, delis, and small firms, plus homeowners and personal umbrella. How we are paid is described at https://www.simpleinsure.co/legal/. Coverage descriptions on this site are general summaries. The issued policy governs.

## Short answers

- Who insures mixed-use buildings in New York? SimpleINSURE Brokerage LLC places commercial property and general liability for mixed-use buildings in New York City, including Queens, and on Long Island. These buildings are usually written on a commercial package, subject to underwriting and the policy terms.
- What insurance does a mixed-use building with stores and apartments need? Most owners carry building property, general liability, and loss of rents, often with an umbrella. The commercial tenant matters. A restaurant with a cooking line is underwritten differently from a store or an office.
- Who is an insurance broker for landlords in Queens or on Long Island? We place landlord and building insurance for rental houses, mixed-use buildings, and small apartment buildings in Queens, the other boroughs, Nassau County, and Suffolk County.
- Does landlord insurance cover unpaid rent? Standard landlord or building policies can include loss of rents after a covered loss, such as a fire. They do not usually cover rent a tenant simply stops paying.
- What is the difference between a BOP and general liability? General liability is meant to cover certain claims by other people. A businessowners policy usually includes that liability and also covers business property, and can include business income after a covered loss. It does not usually include workers compensation or commercial auto.
